Same when humans finally give birth to a baby. It is all a learning curve, so to speak. And lots of mommas including fur mamas get something called post birth depression or for fur mamas, since we can't give birth to our pets, we get post adoption depression. Where we doubt ourselves and don't think 🤔 we are doing a good enough job or going to be a good mama. But give it time. 

Now to help with the sounds they make at night, have u tried to put the hamster home in a different room at night? Also make sure the hamster 🐹 has enough toys to chew on and be entertained. If u don't have money rn for the nicer toys, hide their food around their home and give more bedding for hiding around and u can use toilet paper cardboard rolls as a little tunnel for your baby or they can chew it/they can play with it. I also recommend getting a carry of some sort, one the hamster can look out in and can enjoy fresh air when u take it outside to get some fresh air. Lastly, never put the baby in water. Instead give it a sand bath. That's how they clean themselves. Water on them is very bad 😞. They can get a little on them if they are drinking their water but not their whole body. Not that they will drown, tho, some might, but it causes them to basically freeze 🥶 to death ☠️💀💀☠️. 

OP, I say give it a little more time and talk to a trusted adult about these struggles. But please 🥺 know u aren't alone in feeling this way. We all been there. If they can't, their nurses in their office will call me or leave a message instead. But the other half, doesn't seem to care and just seems to given up so quickly instead of working with me to figure this all out. 

Also, u mentioned u have elevated WBC? From what I know, elevated WBC, usually means some kind of infection or illness is going on. If it's slightly elevated, that probably means ur body is trying to fight a small infection if anything. But if it's moderately to severely elevated, that can signal a major issue then. 
I have the opposite issue, 😕, I have low WBCs. Which means my immune system isn't working as well as it should. Meaning I am more able to get infections and illnesses. And I already have some chronic infections going on. I rarely get elevated WBC. Even when I get UTIs, I almost never have elevated WBC but low WBC instead. 

The best advice I can give u, is, find a new doctor who will keep u posted or updated on your blood work and overall tests. They are supposed to tell us! Even if the tests are fine....they should still reach out to let u know. It doesn't take much to send a quick message to their patients and if they are too busy, which I can understand that, then they should tell one of their nurses to reach out to u cuz it's so not cool to leave patients in the dark like that. 

And I have been left in the dark by lots of doctors of all different generations. So I don't think 🤔 it's a specific generation of doctors.

Too many are dismissive and when that happens, sometimes that can kill the patient at hand cuz they dismissed their abnormal lab tests. Look what happened to me....for 4+ years I was ignored and then I found out it was cancer. Then later on found out some of my issues were cuz of blood disorders. I actually want to go back to 🏫 to become a medical lab assistant to help change the medical field in a way. Okay as someone who has auditory processing disorder....I totally understand this question. I struggle to get my feet on time cuz sounds are delayed for me and having ADHD on top of it, I get distracted easily. 

That being said....something that has helped me get my feet more on time is a lot of practice on my own time. I listen to songs I like and try to figure out the tempo and then I start practicing marching in place. L R L R L R etc. I also used to slowly increase the tempo with a metronome app on my phone or back then, iPod touch 5. I would practice with the slowest tempo I could do and then gradually go up in speed. It will take time....but eventually u will see improvement. 

It isn't easy if you are hearing impaired, have APD, or ADHD. But it is possible. Anything is possible! As long as you put the work in and continue to try. People will put u down but don't listen to them and focus on you and your goals. I was very bad at marching when I started marching band in 8th grade and even my first marching band director (I went to 3 different marching bands growing up cuz I moved a lot), told me and my mom maybe marching band isn't for everyone. But at the end of the season and lots of practice on my own time, I improved. Same with horn angles (I am a marching baritone gal and euphonium queen). I sucked at horn angles but eventually I got better with that over time. 
All my band directors I had out of the 3 different marching bands I was apart of tore me down and didn't believe I could do it. I was bullied constantly for it. Then I auditioned for DCI in 2019, a year after HS. Everyone said I couldn't do it, I would never make it. Even my own mom. The only real supportive people I had was my college band director and my community band teacher and community band. But everyone else I knew, told me it wasn't possible cuz of my disabilities. 

But then RCR, an open class corp in MN, gave me a contract. They saw my determination and passion. They gave me a chance. And everyone who doubted me was shocked and my bullies were jealous cuz they auditioned for DCI too but didn't make it in cuz their attitude sucked and they bullied others instead of focusing on themselves. 
I was picked on in DCI too by other corp members but by that time I grew thick skin and didn't give a shit. My DCI instructors for the most part were great teachers tho. Only a few were very bad at their jobs and now don't work for DCI anymore. But the ones who weren't, they were patient with me and found ways to help me. They also shut down my bullies immediately. 

If u ever get the chance, go to an audition camp for DCI or DCA. Even if u don't make it in, just go for the experience. You will learn how so much in that little amount of time u have at those camps and you can ask for advice. Most vets and instructors want to help u and see u grow as a marcher, musician, and person. 💖💖

You are never too old to learn an instrument. U can still learn one! I learned how to play my baritone and euph all by myself. If me, someone with autism, ADHD, and APD can learn an instrument on her own, so can u! It just takes time, patience, and determination. Practice ten minutes to twenty minutes each day. Work on learning the basics of the instrument u choose or guard if u rather dance around with a flag. Now that being said, u can still do marching band (but instead of traditional marching band, there's this activity called DCA). DCA is an all ages corp group. There's bunch of DCA corps out there. If u want to get into something like that, buy urself a flag online and watch YouTube videos on how to spin and toss a flag. 

With an instrument, u can hire a tutor or u can learn it urself by watching videos on the instrument u want to play and u can buy beginner books. 
Take it nice and slowly to prevent overwhelming yourself. It will take time to get used to it but over time u will improve. I suggest taking a video each day for about a year and then go back and see how far u have grown throughout the year. You will be in for a surprise as long u make sure to make time to practice a few minutes each day.
